question: Can an LLM answer closed-book knowledge questions more accurately if it first recites a relevant passage from its own memory instead of retrieving from a corpus?
hypothesis: Encouraging the model to explicitly recite a specific knowledge source before answering will help augment its memory, and diversifying the recitation helps because several sources can answer the same question.
contributions: RECITE: recite-and-answer paradigm for closed-book QA
Self-consistency over sampled recitations and multiple-recite-and-answer for multi-hop
Passage hint-based diversified recitation with fine-tuning on few-shot-generated questions
Results on four LLMs and three CBQA tasks

method.summary: Few-shot prompt an LLM to write a recitation passage for the question, then answer conditioned on it; sample 20 recitations with top-k sampling and majority-vote the answers. For NQ, a PaLM-62B is also fine-tuned on synthetic question-passage-hint data so it can sample passage hints and greedily recite each.

models.name: UL2-20B
models.tokenizer: SentencePiece, no newline so ' ; ' used as separator

models.name: Codex (code-davinci-002)
models.params: unknown (Table 7 lists GPT-3 175.0B as an educational guess)

training.objective: fine-tune PaLM-62B on synthetic question to passage hint and passage content (only the NQ diversified-recitation variant trains)

inference.decoding: recitations by top-k sampling, answers greedy; passage-hint variant: sample hints, de-duplicate, greedy decode each passage; majority vote over answers
inference.samples: 20 recitations per question (self-consistency); Fig 4 uses random subsets of 20 five times; Table 6 uses 5 seeds of random exemplars
inference.prompting: NQ 5-shot and 64-shot (UL2 16-shot); TriviaQA 5-shot; HotpotQA 4-shot; exemplars separated by three newlines, components by two
inference.retrieval: none for RECITE; BM25 top-1 baseline in Table 3

eval.protocol: Single evaluation per setting except Table 6 (5 exemplar seeds, mean and std) and Fig 4 (5 random subsets); no significance test

availability.weights: UL2-20B and OPT-30B public; Codex via API; PaLM not released

limits: Updating time-sensitive knowledge for a pure LLM method requires training or fine-tuning on the new corpus, which can be costly (Sec 5).
Ethics: all intermediate steps are generated by the LLM, so RECITE may enhance biases in model weights compared to RAG.
Sampling temperature, top-k value and max length are not stated.
TriviaQA and HotpotQA evaluated on only the first 1,024 questions; NQ uses test or dev depending on labels; no significance tests.
Diversified recitation is evaluated only on NQ with PaLM-62B, which is not publicly available.
Gain on TriviaQA for PaLM-62B is 0.46 EM; authors hypothesise trivia questions carry context that weakens recitation for strong LLMs.
Only three closed-book QA tasks; fact checking left to future work.
